Every phone, tablet and computer shows the browser's certificate warning once; continue past it (Advanced, then Proceed / visit this website / Accept the Risk) and the device remembers. To be sure it is this server, compare the certificate fingerprint above with the one in the browser's certificate details or the container log (docker logs sentry-six-manager). If a device that continued before warns again and you changed nothing here, don't continue.

No warning at all: install the certificate authority on a device instead (download it below and compare its fingerprint before trusting it). It can only vouch for local names and private IP addresses.

You opened this page as other.local, which the certificate does not cover, so it warns even on devices with the certificate authority installed.
How to install the certificate authority
  • iPhone / iPad: open the download in Safari, then Settings > General > VPN & Device Management to install it, and Settings > General > About > Certificate Trust Settings to turn on full trust.
  • Android: Settings > Security > Encryption & credentials > Install a certificate > CA certificate.
  • Windows: open the file > Install Certificate > Local Machine > Trusted Root Certification Authorities.
  • macOS: open it in Keychain Access (System), then set Trust to Always Trust.
  • Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Certificates > View Certificates > Authorities > Import.

The IP addresses or names you type in the browser to reach this server; only devices with the certificate authority installed need them. Saving makes a new certificate, so devices that continued past the warning see it once more. Names from TLS_HOSTNAMES: none.
